column2: A benchmark suite of quantum circuits written in OpenQASM, from Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, covering small to large circuits for testing compilers, simulators and hardware.
An application-based benchmark suite for quantum computers, created by Super.tech (later part of Infleqtion), that scores hardware on circuits drawn from real application areas.
Advanced Real-Time Infrastructure for Quantum physics: an open-source Python-based control system from M-Labs for running experiments with precise timing, widely used with trapped ions.
column3: Artiq is also the name of an Inuit spirit in mythology.

column2: An open-source Python framework, begun by Microsoft and the University of Copenhagen, for controlling lab instruments and recording measurement data in quantum experiments.
An open-source family of control electronics, including FPGA controllers and signal sources, designed to run with ARTIQ in atomic physics and trapped-ion labs.
An open-source Python toolkit from Unitary Foundation for quantum error mitigation, providing ZNE, PEC, Clifford data regression and more, working with several quantum SDKs.
A Qiskit add-on for readout error mitigation that corrects measurement errors using only the bit strings actually observed, making it scale to many qubits.
Software that automates probabilistic error cancellation: it learns a device's noise, then generates and weights the many randomized circuit variants PEC needs.
The error suppression and mitigation options built into IBM's Qiskit Runtime service, such as readout correction, dynamical decoupling, ZNE and PEC, selected with simple settings.
Software that automates zero-noise extrapolation: it creates noise-amplified versions of a circuit, for example by gate folding, runs them and extrapolates to zero noise.
An open-source Python library for decoding quantum error-correcting codes, such as the surface code, with fast minimum-weight perfect matching.
A very fast open-source simulator by Craig Gidney for stabilizer (Clifford) circuits, widely used to simulate and study quantum error correction.
QuEra's software for programming neutral-atom quantum computers, including analog Hamiltonian simulation with Rydberg atoms, available for Python and Julia.
Google's open-source Python framework for writing, optimizing and running quantum circuits, designed around the details of near-term hardware.
NVIDIA's open-source platform for hybrid quantum-classical programming in C++ and Python, with GPU-accelerated simulation and support for many quantum hardware backends.
D-Wave's open-source Python tools for formulating optimization problems, such as QUBOs, and solving them on quantum annealers or classical solvers.
A specification for describing quantum programs at the level of control pulses, such as microwave waveforms, instead of gates. It is part of the OpenQASM ecosystem.
Open Quantum Assembly Language: a widely used text format for quantum circuits, created at IBM. Version 3 adds classical control, timing and pulses.
Xanadu's open-source Python library for quantum machine learning and differentiable programming, connecting quantum circuits to libraries such as PyTorch and JAX.
An open-source Python framework for quantum computing started at ETH Zurich, with a compiler that translates high-level programs to various backends.
Rigetti's Python library for writing Quil programs and running them on Rigetti's quantum processors or simulators.
An open-source Python library for rewriting and simplifying quantum circuits using the ZX-calculus, often reducing gate counts.
An open-source full-stack framework for quantum computing, led by the Technology Innovation Institute (Abu Dhabi), covering simulation, hardware control and calibration.
IBM's open-source software development kit for quantum computing, the most widely used. It covers building circuits, transpiling them and running them on simulators or IBM hardware.
A high-level open-source quantum programming framework from Fraunhofer FOKUS that works with variables and functions instead of individual gates and qubits.
Microsoft's toolkit for quantum programming, including the Q# language, simulators and resource estimation tools.
QIR: a common intermediate format for quantum programs based on LLVM, led by Microsoft and the QIR Alliance, so different languages can target different hardware.
Quantum Instruction Language: Rigetti's low-level language for quantum programs, with classical memory and control.
A functional quantum programming language embedded in Haskell, designed for describing large, complex quantum algorithms.
A high-level quantum programming language from ETH Zurich that automatically uncomputes temporary values, avoiding a common source of errors.
Xanadu's open-source Python library for photonic, continuous-variable quantum computing, used to design and simulate optical circuits.
A Google library that combines Cirq circuits with TensorFlow, for building hybrid quantum-classical machine learning models.
Quantinuum's quantum software development kit and compiler, used through Python as pytket, which optimizes circuits for many types of hardware.
The high-performance simulator package for Qiskit, able to simulate circuits with realistic noise models on CPUs and GPUs.
Google's fast open-source state-vector simulator, written in C++ and used with Cirq.
The Quantum Exact Simulation Toolkit: an open-source, high-performance simulator from the University of Oxford that runs on laptops, GPUs and supercomputers.
A fast open-source quantum circuit simulator from Japan, written in C++ with a Python interface, popular for variational algorithm research.
The Quantum Toolbox in Python: an open-source library for simulating the dynamics of open quantum systems, widely used in physics research.
A companion tool to Stim that runs large batches of error-correction simulations in parallel and collects statistics, such as logical error rates.
